name: Bedan
title: Judge in Israel
summary: Bedan is a figure mentioned in Samuel's speech to the people of Israel, where he is counted among the deliverers God sent to rescue Israel from their enemies. His identity is disputed; some scholars identify him with Barak or Samson, while others see him as a separate judge. He is also mentioned in 1 Chronicles as a descendant of Manasseh.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Samuel's farewell speech
keyEvents.description: Samuel mentions Bedan as one of the deliverers God sent to rescue Israel from their enemies, along with Jerubbaal (Gideon) and Jephthah.

keyEvents.title: Descendant of Manasseh
keyEvents.description: In 1 Chronicles, a Bedan is mentioned as the son of Ulam, a descendant of Machir, the son of Manasseh. It is uncertain whether this is the same person.

keyEvents.title: Part of God's story of salvation
keyEvents.description: Samuel's speech places Bedan in the line of God's chosen instruments who delivered Israel during the time of the judges, and shows God's faithfulness to His people despite their unfaithfulness.

keyEvents.title: Context: Israel's cry for help
keyEvents.description: Bedan was raised up in response to Israel's prayer for deliverance after they had abandoned the Lord and served Baal and Ashtoreth.
